headline: The clap suites all run on real bytes now — last synth-mic retired
lede: Chrome 157 silently deafened every suite that faked its microphone through WebAudio. Plaicraft's clap test was the last holdout; it now records through Chrome's fake capture device fed by baked WAVs, so consent, recorder, clocks and uploads are the exact production path on real opus bytes.

notes.text: #2709 closed: claptestplay migrated to fake-file capture (#2723) — one launch per clap schedule, phone storage carried across relaunches so the teach/learn/re-arm story stays one device.

Root cause found the hard way: recording:true stamps at seed-birth, but a real mic opens milliseconds later — reads between those two instants aimed taps at nothing. Every take now anchors on the take clock's own zero.
The fake device replays its file from position 0 at every mic-open — measured, and now pinned by a permanent micprobe check, so any future engine change says so before a suite bleeds.
Clean suite 52/52 with honest contention SKIPs; breaking the stamp pipe turns it red and exits 1 — the harness still proves it can fail.
